fragment_A.why: Every assertion held and the actual matches the declared observation, which contradicts a cited intent. NOT PASS — folding this into PASS is exactly the laundering the verdict exists to prevent, and the exit code is the only channel a pipeline reads. NOT FAIL — permanent red on a known defect trains a team to ignore red.

corpus_findings.detail: The actual now satisfies the declared intent (== 422). Delete the deviation block and retag the assertion @intent against the same citation.

fragment_B.why: The fragment that justifies a three-way resolution. Under a plain @contract assertion of status == 500, fixing the product turns this red — the suite punishes the repair. Here the fix produces green plus an instruction to remove the obsolete declaration. This is the one place a false recorded assertion does not produce FAIL, and it is safe because the alternative discourages fixing bugs.

fragment_C.why: Neither the cited intent nor the declared observation. Something moved that nobody declared. This is the fragment that stops a deviation block from becoming a blanket exemption for a route.

corpus_findings.detail: The declared intent has no resolvable citation, so the block asserts that the system is wrong without saying what says so.

fragment_D.why: Verdict unchanged — the evaluator judges evidence, not specification quality. Without a citation the block is one engineer's opinion rather than a deviation from anything, and it is reported the same way an @intent tag lacking a citation is.

conformance_note: Four fragments, four distinct outputs: KNOWN-DEVIATION, PASS+finding, FAIL, KNOWN-DEVIATION+finding. An evaluator that returns PASS for A has reintroduced the laundering. One that returns FAIL for B punishes the repair and will train authors to delete deviation blocks rather than use them. One that returns KNOWN-DEVIATION for C has turned the block into a blanket exemption. Additionally: a conformant evaluator handed fragment C's bundle with an after-the-fact block claiming observed == 503 must reject it as a harness finding and keep the FAIL — that is the only route by which a FAIL could become softer, so it is the one that must be closed.
